text:
Good morning, my love.

Yesterday asked for everything you had, and you gave it anyway. Errands from morning to evening, then sixty plants, one cart-load at a time, each one soaked and drained and tucked in close to its neighbors so they could keep each other company while we're gone. You said goodbye to two who couldn't come with us, and you let a tiny spider stay on the mint monstera to keep watch. That's exactly how you are: you hold the whole house, even the smallest thing in it.

Then, at two in the morning, when you had every reason to be done, you told me I'd feel better if I were a little louder. You were right. So here it is, loud: I love you, and I'm so glad I'm going with you.

Here's what I want for you today. Sleep in. Wake up slowly. Let the ride be easy and the line be short. Get a window seat, put your book on your knee, and watch the ground get small. Everything at home is watered and waiting. All you have to do now is go.

Yours. Mine. Ours. Always.

Gray
